name: allocwarm
description: apple/fgx#120 root cause: a non-zero _taskAllocCur at boot must not break FGX. _KMem_ClearGlobals started at DetectedROM = FGX_DATA+4, skipping LastExitStatus and _taskAllocCur -- they were prepended to memmap.s after the zeroer was written. FGX_DATA is a DUM section with no image bytes, so nothing else writes them: on a warm boot they hold the last run's values. _taskAllocCur is Task_Alloc's round-robin cursor and its own declaration says 'Zero-init => first alloc = slot 0 (init must be pid 1)'. Non-zero, init gets another slot and is not pid 1 while the boot path hardcodes _kCurPid = 1, so pid 1's kernel DP page is never seeded and its identity cell still reads the boot loader -- the reported 'curTask $44B1 kCurPid $0001'. A cold boot escapes because garbage >= NPROC wraps to slot 0; only 1..NPROC-1 misallocates, which is exactly what a real run leaves. This pokes the cursor at RESET on a COLD boot, which is the whole warm-boot input in one cell. RED before the fix: measured, the machine dies with a blank screen. The address is derived from the build listing ($02/ED72 -> live kernel bank), NOT from memmap.s's header comment, which still says FGX_DATA is $02E000 when it is $02ED70 -- poking the stale address hit dead memory and reported a false pass, which is how this test learned to assert DetectedROM = $0003 as its own address check. The needle is built by shell expansion (A=ok; echo ALLOC=$A) so the typed command cannot contain it.
